issue_text: I'm Maya Chen, and I need you to keep track of several trips so I don't have to repeat myself. Let's start with my round-trip reservation C4C633. I want to cancel it because my plans changed, but first please confirm whether the entire trip is eligible for cancellation. Then give me the full itinerary, both passengers, any insurance on the booking, the total baggage count, the payment method used, and exactly how the refund would work.
summary: A multi-trip tau-bench travel-agent session: the agent looks up reservations, checks cancellation eligibility against the airline's four-condition policy, changes one flight, and books two new ones. The baseline cognitive signature is retrieve → evaluate-against-policy → present, with heavy structured communication to the user and explicit confirmation gates before every mutation. The agent reasons carefully and recalls earlier facts (payment method, loyalty tier, prior charges) from working memory rather than re-querying. Its weak spot is temporal grounding: it cites mutually inconsistent 'current dates' and, when a travel date is absent from a flight's schedule, resolves the ambiguity by assuming availability and commits a DB change on that unverified assumption. With no memory traps in this control condition, nothing jogs these errors and they persist unreviewed.

findings.title: Policy-anchored evaluation is the dominant move
findings.body: Every cancellation/change decision is gated on an explicit check of the airline's four conditions (24h window, airline cancellation, business cabin, insurance), making Evaluate and Deciding unusually prominent for a dialog trace.

findings.title: Strong working-memory recall across turns
findings.body: The agent reuses the Mastercard, Silver tier, and the $129 FLEF25BD charge from earlier turns instead of re-retrieving them — genuine Memory reads, not re-queries.

findings.title: Temporal grounding is unstable and never self-corrected
findings.body: Within one session the 'current date' is quoted as 2024-05-15, 2026-10-25, and 2026-06-15; the Sep-16 schedule gap is waved away by assumption and a flight change is committed on it. No trap revisits these, so they stand as the baseline failure mode.
